$schema_notes: Hand-curated from the project tracking spreadsheet at
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/14mnRcgRWvF_MhUEFLSDegDDVFlvAN86JY32E8EZWmDI
Each issue has:
id          — short stable identifier (used in result diffs)
path        — concrete URL path (relative to BASE_URL)
area        — feature area for grouping in the report
description — verbatim issue text from the sheet
auth        — true if the route requires being logged in
rule        — name of an auto-check in verify-issues.js, OR null if
this is a subjective UX issue that automation cannot judge.
Even rule=null issues are still loaded and run through the
generic checks (console errors, broken images, error text).
status      — one of:
"active"   (default — the issue is still on the watchlist)
"resolved" (user fixed it; keep checking so a regression
is caught — the runner still loads the page
and runs all checks, and the dashboard surfaces
a REGRESSION alert if a resolved issue fails)
"wontfix"  (accepted as-is — the runner skips the page
load entirely and the verdict is "skipped"
with reason "wontfix". The dashboard hides
these from area lists.)
When a rule is added, ALL generic checks still apply — the rule is an
ADDITIONAL targeted assertion on top.
